_comment: Mutation measurement of the UI. Started as two files, picked so the run answers two different questions rather than producing one blended number; src/hooks/useFeatureToggle.js was added later because it writes a persisted admin setting and a mutant that inverted the value it posts, or dropped the failure branch, would leave a switch silently doing the opposite of what it shows. It runs against its own renderHook test, which touches nothing outside app/ui and so is safe in the sandbox. src/auth/usePermissions.js is the client-side permission gate: seven components import it, NO test file imported it before this pilot, and its 39% line coverage was incidental — whatever happened to execute while other components rendered. src/utils/matrixFilter.js is the opposite case: 99% coverage with its own dedicated test file, so its score says whether that number was earned. Enforced: see MUTATION FLOOR below. Run: cd app/ui && npm run test:mutation. MUTATOR SET: everything enabled, which is DELIBERATELY different from app/api/stryker.auth.config.json. There, StringLiteral and ObjectLiteral were disabled because permissions.js is largely a catalog of human-readable labels and mutating that prose produced 68 of 72 survivors while saying nothing about behaviour. Here the string literals ARE the behaviour: 'admin.auth' is the permission a hook checks for, and 'rows-as-resources' is a value the normaliser accepts — a wrong one silently grants or drops. Those mutants are worth killing, so they stay in. Do not copy the API's exclusions here without re-reading this. THE 10 REMAINING SURVIVORS ARE ANALYSED, NOT UNEXAMINED, and are left visible rather than declared away (the floor sits below the measured score, so they cost nothing): (a) 7 of them are the delimiters inside matrixFilter's `canonical()` -- '[' ',' ']' '{' ':' '}'. Both sides of any fingerprint comparison run through the SAME mutated serializer, so killing one needs two structurally different filters that collide once a delimiter is dropped. JSON.stringify escapes every string it emits, so the quote pattern needed to forge a collision cannot be produced by any value a filter can hold. (b) `Array.isArray(obj) -> false` serialises arrays as index-keyed objects; no filter field can hold either an array or a plain object depending on input (`list()` returns [] for a non-array, normalizeSort always returns an array), so the two shapes never meet in the same slot. (c) `typeof f === 'object' -> true` in normalizeMatrixFilter leaves `f ? f : EMPTY_FILTER`: a truthy non-object (string, number, boolean) has none of the sixteen filter fields on it, so every field falls back and the result is EMPTY_FILTER either way. (d) `permissions.size === 0 -> false` in usePermissions drops a redundant fast path -- an empty Set reaches `.some()` and returns false regardless. Re-check (a) and (b) if canonical() ever stops delegating to JSON.stringify. MUTATION FLOOR: `break` is set a few points under the measured score, and is a RATCHET — it only ever goes up. It is enforced by the weekly .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml (never on a PR: mutation is far heavier than the unit suite). The margin is not slack to spend, it absorbs the two things that legitimately move a score without anyone editing a test: a Stryker/vitest upgrade that changes which mutants are generated, and timeouts, which count as killed and can flip under CI load. Raise the floor when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green — a drop means a test stopped discriminating. Measured 95.6% when the floor was raised to 93. The shared crawler-wizard layer (saveCrawlerConfig + useCrawlerSave/useCredentialFields/useCrawlerDiscovery) joined at 97.1%, and useFeatureToggle.js sits at 100%; the ten analysed survivors below are unchanged and all belong to the original two files. src/utils/attributeLabels.js JOINED THIS SCOPE (issue #872) — the session cache behind every clean attribute name on screen and in the xlsx export. It belongs with matrixFilter.js rather than in a scope of its own: same shape (a small pure-ish util with its own dedicated test file), and the workflow's scope matrix plus the report merge in tools/mutation/stryker_to_mutation_json.py both derive from these configs, so a new config with no matrix entry would fail the weekly publish rather than measure anything. Its own hook, src/hooks/useAttributeLabels.js, is measured and then EXCLUDED — see mutationExclusions below for the numbers. First measurement 77.14%, and the six survivors were all real gaps rather than equivalents: the null-key guard, the ext.-prefix ANCHOR (an unanchored strip mutant survived, i.e. nothing pinned that `ext.` is a prefix and not a substring), the non-object-payload guard, and the initial `loaded = false` — that last one invisible to every existing case because they all start with resetAttributeLabels(), so a module that woke up believing it had already loaded would never fetch and no test would notice. Tests for all four landed; the file now scores 94.29% and the scope 93.88% over 196 mutants. FLOOR at the time STAYED 91 (since raised to 93): the score is where it was (93.8 -> 93.88) but over a wider, differently-weighted mutant set, and 91 keeps the margin the paragraph above says it is for. The two remaining survivors in that file are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT and left visible rather than silenced: `{ labels: {} } -> {}` on a non-ok response feeds setAttributeLabels an undefined map, which builds the same empty null-prototype object; and emptying the `.finally` that nulls `inflight` is unreachable, because every settle path sets `loaded`, after which loadAttributeLabels returns at its `if (loaded)` guard and never reads `inflight` again. Re-check both if a retry or a cache invalidation is ever added. SCOPE GREW FOR #1166 and the label 'permissions + filter' is now too narrow: this config is the UI's PURE-LOGIC scope — the modules that decide something, hold no JSX, and have their own dedicated test file. src/components/shared/sharedSnapshot.js and src/hooks/useHashPage.js joined on those terms. Both belong here rather than in the hooks configs specifically because their string literals ARE behaviour, which is the one thing that makes this config different: 'rotated' / 'rollup' / 'grid' / 'rows-as-subjects' are the values a share round-trips through the database, and 'dashboard' is the route a bare hash falls back to — a wrong one silently shows a recipient a different view than the sharer saw. Adding them costs the weekly run little: neither renders anything, so their mutants pay for two more small non-jsdom test files, not for a mount. Keep that admission test when adding a file here — a React component belongs in a mount-test-backed config or in the exclusions below, not in this one. MATRIX SHARING WENT BEHIND A FEATURE FLAG (#1166): src/hooks/useCanShareMatrix.js joined on the same admission test — no JSX, its own test file — and because its literals are behaviour: 'matrixSharing' is the flag and 'data.share' the permission every sharing control asks about, and `=== true` is what keeps a truthy non-boolean from opening the feature. SEC-2026-09 H-07: src/auth/authFetchHeaders.js joined on the same admission test — no JSX, its own test file — and because its literals are behaviour: 'X-Requested-With: IdentityAtlas' is the exact marker the API accepts as a same-app request, and the order of the merge decides whether a caller can override the signed-in token. SAVING AND SHARING BECAME ONE EXPERIENCE (#1202): src/components/matrix/shareState.js joined the mutate list on this config's admission test — no JSX, its own dedicated test file, and literals that ARE behaviour. It is the single answer to “is this matrix saved, and is it shared?” for the matrix bar, the wizard's Save/Share step and Admin, so a wrong answer is wrong in three places at once: 'person' versus 'people' is the label all three print, `!s.revokedAt` is what keeps a revoked link from making a matrix read as shared, and the fingerprint comparison is what lets a matrix that was only folded or drilled still recognise itself. Its five new sibling components are excluded with reasons below rather than mutated, on the same rule the #1166 entries follow: each one's decision was deliberately moved INTO shareState.js or useCanShareMatrix.js, both of which are mutated here, and what is left in them is chrome. src/components/matrix/ShareMatrixButton.jsx left the exclusions because the file is gone — #1202 replaced the toolbar's second share control with the single one on the Load / Save / Share bar. THE WIZARD BECAME FOUR STEPS (#1202): src/components/matrix/saveStepState.js (what the Save & share step's one primary button says and does) and src/components/matrix/matrixRequests.js (how the save and share surfaces read a refusal, and recognise a name clash) joined the mutate list on this config's admission test — no JSX, a dedicated test file each, and literals that are behaviour: 'Save changes & show' versus 'Show matrix' is whether a click writes to a matrix other people see, and 409 is what routes an error onto the name field. The step components they serve are excluded with reasons below. Their test files, and shareState.test.js / sortStepState.test.js (in the mutate list before but missing from vitest.stryker.config.js, so their mutants had no killers in the run), were added to that include list. NOT YET MEASURED: a local run on the Windows dev box scored every file 0-6% — including useCanShareMatrix.js, which measures 100% in the weekly workflow — so that run says nothing, and the first weekly run is the measurement for both new files. WHO CHANGED A SAVED MATRIX: src/components/matrix/matrixHistoryText.js joined the mutate list on this config's admission test — no JSX, its own dedicated test file, and literals that ARE behaviour. It is the wording of the matrix History trail: "saved this matrix" versus "changed it" is whether a person is being named as the author of a matrix or of an edit to one, the fallback for an unknown actor is what stops an event reading as if nobody did it, and the `updatedBy === createdBy` test is what keeps a matrix nobody has touched from claiming its creator changed it. Its dialog, src/components/matrix/MatrixHistoryDialog.jsx, is excluded with a reason below on the rule the #1202 entries follow. A MATRIX THAT STOPPED WORKING: src/components/matrix/matrixHealth.js joined the mutate list on this config's admission test — no JSX, its own dedicated test file, and literals that are behaviour. It is the sentence a broken matrix says about itself, and it inflects four ways at once ("context/contexts", "exists/exist", "that condition was/those conditions were"), so a mutant that flips a plural boundary ships prose that reads as wrong to the person being asked to fix it. Its two guards matter more: `> 0` is what decides whether a marker appears at all, and treating a MISSING missingContextIds field as zero is what keeps a surface that never reported health from marking every matrix broken — a mutant turning that into "unknown means faulty" cries wolf everywhere. Its two components, BrokenMatrixBadge.jsx and MatrixEmptyState.jsx, are excluded with reasons below on the rule the #1202 entries follow.

The amber marker on a saved matrix that names a context somebody deleted. It decides nothing: isMatrixBroken and brokenMatrixTitle in ./matrixHealth.js, mutated above, decide whether it appears and what it says, and the component is the span that renders them. One component rather than a badge per list, so the marker cannot mean one thing in 'Open a matrix' and another in the name menu; both hosts are asserted (OpenMatrixList.mount.test.jsx, MatrixNameBar.mount.test.jsx) with a broken and a healthy matrix side by side, and MatrixEmptyState.mount.test.jsx pins that a healthy row renders nothing at all.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/MatrixEmptyState.j: What an empty matrix says, shared by all three views so a matrix that broke explains itself the same way whichever way round it is read. The only decision — is there an explanation to add, or does the caller keep its plain empty state — is brokenMatrixExplanation() in ./matrixHealth.js, mutated above; what is left is the message and an amber paragraph. Both branches are asserted in MatrixEmptyState.mount.test.jsx, and MatrixView.mount.test.jsx drives the same empty result with and without a deleted context, which is what separates a broken matrix from a correctly empty one.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/MatrixHistoryDialo: The History trail of a saved matrix: a fetch of /api/matrix/saved-filters/:id/history and a list of what came back. Every sentence it prints is ./matrixHistoryText.js, which IS mutated above, and the events themselves are built server-side in routes/matrix/savedFilterHistory.js, mutation-tested in app/api/stryker.matrix.config.json. What is left here is the modal and the loop over the events. Its one branch of its own — a matrix with no recorded changes says history is only kept from a point in time, rather than showing an empty list that would read as 'nobody ever changed it' — is asserted in MatrixHistoryDialog.mount.test.jsx, along with the trail being read for the matrix the dialog was opened on.
mutationExclusions.src/utils/crawlerMetaRegistry.js: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and this module resolves crawler metadata with import.meta.glob over ../../../tools/crawlers/*/CrawlerMeta.js — a path that does not exist in the sandbox. The glob would resolve to nothing there, so the dry run fails before a single mutant is evaluated (same constraint documented in vitest.stryker.config.js). Its selectors are unit-tested in src/utils/crawlerMetaRegistry.test.js — against injected fixtures for the branch logic AND against the real discovered registry, which is what catches an experimental flag being dropped from a CrawlerMeta.js.
mutationExclusions.src/components/CrawlersPage.SelectType.j: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and this module resolves crawler metadata with import.meta.glob over ../../../tools/crawlers/*/CrawlerMeta.js — a path that does not exist in the sandbox. The glob would resolve to nothing there, so the dry run fails before a single mutant is evaluated (same constraint documented in vitest.stryker.config.js). It imports crawlerMetaRegistry.js, so it inherits that. Presentational besides: its one decision (offer experimental types or not) is selectableCrawlerTypes(), mutation-relevant logic that lives in the excluded module above and is covered by CrawlersPage.SelectType.test.jsx mounting the real picker.
mutationExclusions.src/components/admin/ExperimentalFeature: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and this module resolves crawler metadata with import.meta.glob over ../../../tools/crawlers/*/CrawlerMeta.js — a path that does not exist in the sandbox. The glob would resolve to nothing there, so the dry run fails before a single mutant is evaluated (same constraint documented in vitest.stryker.config.js). It imports crawlerMetaRegistry.js, so it inherits that. Mounted end-to-end in ExperimentalFeaturesSection.test.jsx (flag rendering, both toggle directions, the failure path); the flag semantics it drives are mutation-tested server-side in app/api/stryker.features.config.json.
mutationExclusions.src/components/crawler/wizardFields.jsx: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and the tests that assert this component's output are the crawler wizards' own render/e2e tests under tools/crawlers/, which is outside the sandbox — mutating it without its killers present would report false survivors, which is worse than measuring less (the same reasoning as vitest.stryker.config.js's narrow include). Presentational besides: labelled inputs, option lists, the schedule list and the Back/Next row. Its one behavioural rule — label and control stay siblings, because the e2e selects fields with `label:has-text("X") + input` — is asserted by those e2e tests, not by anything mutable here.
Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and the tests that assert this component's output are the crawler wizards' own render/e2e tests under tools/crawlers/, which is outside the sandbox — mutating it without its killers present would report false survivors, which is worse than measuring less (the same reasoning as vitest.stryker.config.js's narrow include). The decision it encodes — which fields each auth method needs — is mirrored by buildCredentialFields/canSubmitCredentials in @ui/utils/crawlerCredentials, and THAT is unit-tested (credentialGating.test.js in the omada and midPoint folders) and mutable. This file only renders the result.
mutationExclusions.src/hooks/useAttributeLabels.js: MEASURED, then excluded on the evidence -- not skipped unexamined. It is a 20-line effect hook that loads the shared label map once per session and forces one re-render; it holds no rule of its own (the extension-prefix rule is server-side, the cache is src/utils/attributeLabels.js, which IS mutated here). Scored 50.00% over 12 mutants, and every one of the 6 survivors is equivalent under that once-per-session contract: `n => n + 1` vs `n => n - 1` vs `n => undefined` in the bump reducer all re-render on the single bump that ever fires; dropping the `alive` unmount guard and emptying the `[authFetch]` dependency list are both invisible because the module-level `loaded` flag already makes a second load a no-op. Killing them would mean asserting React's re-render bookkeeping rather than any behaviour a user can observe, which is the kind of test this repo's testing guide warns produces green ticks and no discrimination. Its actual contract -- first paint shows the raw key, the paint after the map arrives shows the clean name -- is pinned by src/hooks/useAttributeLabels.test.jsx and src/components/attributeLabels.mount.test.jsx. Revisit if the hook ever gains a retry, a refresh trigger, or per-target loading, at which point the bump count and the dependency list start carrying decisions.
mutationExclusions.src/AppRoot.jsx: The root route dispatcher (#1166): one branch — a '#shared:<token>' hash renders the recipient shell, anything else renders App — wrapped in a Suspense fallback. Both halves of that branch are already mutation-tested as pure functions: parseSharedRoute in App.helpers.js and useHashPage.js, which is in the mutate list above. What is left in this file is the lazy() import and the fallback markup, so its mutants would measure JSX, not the routing decision. AppRoot.mount.test.jsx asserts both branches render.
mutationExclusions.src/contexts/SharedViewContext.jsx: A createContext(false) plus the one-line useContext reader that the shared shell flips to hide analyst-only affordances (#1166). There is no decision in the file to mutate — the only meaningful mutant is the default value, and SharedViewContext.mount.test.jsx pins that (a component outside the provider must see analyst chrome) along with each consumer's opt-out.
mutationExclusions.src/components/SharedMatricesPage.jsx: The Admin overview of every share (#1166, extended by #1202): a fetch, a table of rows, one expanded SharePanel at a time, and a revoke confirmation. Its own logic is formatting — 'Never opened' versus a usage count, Active versus Revoked — which is markup-adjacent text a mutant changes without changing behaviour. SharedMatricesPage.mount.test.jsx drives the list, the empty state, the revoke round-trip and the one-row-at-a-time manage toggle; the SQL behind it is contract-tested.
mutationExclusions.src/components/SharedMatrixPage.jsx: The recipient's shell (#1166): resolve the token, then render the matrix or one of the four terminal states. The two decisions it makes are extracted and covered elsewhere — applyDisplayMode (mutated above, in sharedSnapshot.js) folds the stored display mode back into the filter, and the HTTP-status-to-state mapping is asserted per status in SharedMatrixPage.mount.test.jsx. The rest is the bare chrome itself.
mutationExclusions.src/components/inputs/PeoplePicker.jsx: The directory typeahead behind 'Share with' (#1166). Its rules are asserted by inputs that discriminate in PeoplePicker.mount.test.jsx: a row with no sign-in name is offered but disabled, an already-picked person cannot be added twice, removal is by sign-in key, and an unsettled term reads as 'Searching…' rather than 'No people match'. Around those sits a debounced fetch and a chip list, so mutating the file measures mostly Tailwind classes and placeholder prose.
Chrome only (#1166, reworked by #1202): a Modal whose title names the saved matrix being shared when there is one, wrapping SharePanel. Everything sharing IS lives in that panel and in ./shareState.js (mutated above), deliberately, so the matrix bar, the wizard and Admin cannot drift. The one branch here — titled after a saved matrix versus an unsaved one — is asserted in ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/ShareMatrixForm.js: The create half of “share this matrix” (#1166, reworked by #1202). Its decisions are asserted directly in ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx with inputs that discriminate between the two modes: an unsaved matrix must be given a name and at least one recipient before the button enables and POSTs the filter, the managed toggle and the display mode from displayModeOf (mutated above); an already-saved one is never asked for a second name and POSTs only { savedFilterId, recipients } — the exact confusion #1202 was filed about. The server re-checks the recipient rule in shareRecipients.js, which is mutation-tested in app/api. The remainder is the resulting link and its copy affordance.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/WizardShareStep.js: The "Share with" section of the wizard's Save & share step (#1166, reworked twice by #1202): SharePanel for a matrix that is already shared (and not being saved as a copy), otherwise the shared people field — picking people does not share by itself; the wizard's primary button saves and then shares. Its one rule — a matrix too large to LOAD offers no new share, but an existing share is still manageable, because taking somebody off a share must never depend on the matrix being loadable — is asserted on both sides in ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx. What the primary button does is saveStepState.js, mutated above.
mutationExclusions.src/components/shared/SharedMatrixHeader: Presentational header for the recipient's shell (#1166): the product mark, the share's name and a 'Shared matrix' label, with a Back control when a drill-down is open. No data and no decision — the back affordance's behaviour is asserted from the page in SharedMatrixPage.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/shared/SharedMatrixRow.js: One row of the Shared matrices table (#1166, #1202) — name, recipients, usage, the Revoke control and a Manage toggle that expands the shared SharePanel, all rendered from props the page already resolved. Mutating it measures date and count formatting; what the row must SAY for a never-opened and for a revoked share, and that a revoked one offers neither Manage nor Revoke, is asserted in SharedMatricesPage.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/shared/SharedMatrixUnavai: Four static messages for a share that cannot be opened — revoked, unknown, not-for-you, failed (#1166) — and a lookup into that table. The file is deliberately prose: the recipient is a business user who must never see a status code. Mutating the strings would produce survivors that say nothing, which is exactly the permissions.js lesson recorded in the API's auth config.
mutationExclusions.src/contexts/FeaturesContext.jsx: A createContext({}) plus a one-line useContext reader that carries App.jsx's /api/features flags to components deep inside the matrix (#1166). The one meaningful mutant is the default value — `{}`, so every flag reads off outside App — and useCanShareMatrix.test.jsx pins exactly that (no flags supplied → cannot share), with useCanShareMatrix.js itself in the mutate list above.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/MatrixNameBar.jsx: The document half of the strip above the matrix (#768, reworked by #1202): the name menu, the Unsaved changes chip and the Shared with N chip. Everything it DECIDES is imported and mutated: currentSavedMatrix in ./shareState.js answers which saved matrix this is and whether the screen diverged from it, savedMatrixLoadArgs how a load is tagged, sharedWithLabel how the count is spelled, ./useSavedMatrixNaming.js what Rename and Duplicate send, and useCanShareMatrix.js gates the share chip. What is left here is a fetch, a DELETE and the chrome that renders those answers. Its one rule of its own — the list is re-read only when the APPLIED filter actually changed — and every chip condition are driven with discriminating inputs in MatrixNameBar.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/SaveMatrixDialog.j: The “name it and save it” modal (#768/#1202), hosted by the wizard and — as Rename and Duplicate — by the strip's name menu: a labelled field, a 409 shown inline instead of overwriting somebody else's matrix, and an optional “save the change back to <matrix>” block. Its one rule — the author of a SHARED matrix is told who the change reaches before it does — is liveShareWarning() in ./shareState.js, which IS mutated above. What remains is the field, the two buttons and their disabled state, asserted in MatrixNameBar.mount.test.jsx and MatrixFilterWizard.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/SavedMatrixMenu.js: The saved-matrix dropdown (#768/#1202) in its two guises — the strip's name menu and the wizard's loader: the org-wide list with the current matrix marked, an outside-click close, the document verbs and a delete confirmation. The only decision is which confirmation a SHARED matrix gets, and the count inside it comes from sharedWithLabel() in ./shareState.js, mutated above. Mutating this file measures the open/closed bookkeeping and Tailwind classes; the current marker, which verbs appear for a saved versus an unsaved matrix, and that deleting a shared matrix warns about the recipients whose link it closes are asserted in MatrixNameBar.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/OpenMatrixList.jsx: The no-matrix-on-screen state (#1202): a fetch of the saved matrices, a list, New matrix, and the no-data message. The one thing an opened matrix must carry — the tag of the saved matrix it came from, with the governed toggle handed over separately — is savedMatrixLoadArgs() in ./shareState.js, mutated above. What remains is which of four renders applies (no data / unknown / loading / empty / list), each asserted in OpenMatrixList.mount.test.jsx, and formatting.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/SharePanel.jsx: Manage a saved matrix's share in place (#1202) — one panel, hosted identically by the matrix bar, the wizard's Save/Share step and Admin, which is what stops those three becoming three mechanisms. The decision it routes on, “is there a LIVE share for this saved matrix” (a revoked one is history, not a share), is activeShareOf() in ./shareState.js and IS mutated above. What remains is the recipient-list state, two authFetch calls and a confirmation dialog. ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx drives both halves — create when unshared, edit/copy/stop-sharing when shared — and the server re-checks who may open a share in shareRecipients.js, which is mutation-tested in app/api.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/MatrixSortStep.jsx: The Group & sort columns section of the wizard's Layout step (#1202), extracted from MatrixFilterWizard.jsx. Every rule it applies lives in ./sortStepState.js and IS mutated above: which columns may be sorted on (displayName is never one), what 'auto' fold-on-load resolves to against FOLD_AUTO_THRESHOLD, when another sort level is still on offer, and which level an add/update/remove/flip lands on. What is left is the Manager-Hierarchy fetch, the fold checkbox and the markup; mutating it measures Tailwind classes. MatrixFilterWizard.mount.test.jsx drives it through the wizard — attribute vs hierarchy mode, added and flipped levels, and that roll-up disables it.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/wizardControls.jsx: Presentational controls shared by the Matrix wizard's steps (#1202): a choice card, a choice group, a labelled checkbox, a disclosure, a segmented control and a section heading. No decisions — each renders props and reports a click; its only state is a disclosure's open flag. aria-pressed / aria-expanded, which the steps' tests query by, are asserted through MatrixFilterWizard.mount.test.jsx (every choice reports its pressed state, More options starts closed and opens, and starts open when its option is already on).
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/WizardConditionSte: The wizard's Subjects and Resources steps (#1202): the opening either/or choice plus the Include / Exclude condition lists, moved out of MatrixFilterWizard.jsx. The only rule here — which axis the words "Rows are" / "Columns are" name — is axisHeadings() in MatrixFilterWizard.helpers.js; the rest wires clicks to the wizard's mutators. MatrixFilterWizard.mount.test.jsx asserts each choice sets its filter field (rowType, includeBusinessRoles, includeInheritedAccess), that a changed row type clears the subject conditions and an unchanged one does not, and the add/update/remove of attribute and context conditions.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/WizardLayoutStep.j: The wizard's Layout step (#1202): the Group & sort section (disabled with its reason while a roll-up is on), the Roll up section and the Open with section (trends panel, default lens). It holds no rule of its own — roll-up switching is applyRollupMode()/rollupModeOf() in MatrixFilterWizard.helpers.js and the lens values are LENS_VALUES in saveStepState.js — and there is deliberately no orientation control. MatrixFilterWizard.mount.test.jsx asserts that grouping disables under a roll-up and re-enables when it is switched off, that the lens and the trends checkbox reach onApply, and that no step offers an orientation control.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/WizardRollupSectio: The Layout step's Roll up section (#1202): Off / By attribute / By context, the attribute select or context picker, and the content/cell-value cards once on. The decisions — which mode a filter is in, what switching mode clears (the hierarchy sort, the drill state) and which attribute By attribute starts on — are rollupModeOf()/applyRollupMode() in MatrixFilterWizard.helpers.js with their own unit tests. MatrixFilterWizard.mount.test.jsx drives each mode to onApply (rollup, rollupKind, rollupContextId, rollupContent, rollupMetric) and MatrixFilterWizard.contentStep.test.jsx pins the content cards' defaults.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/WizardSaveStep.jsx: The fields of the wizard's Save & share step (#1202): name with its inline error, the description disclosure, the save-as-copy link and — for a user who may share — the Share with section. What the one primary button says and does is saveStepState.js (mutated above) and the requests are useWizardSave.js; this file renders their state. MatrixFilterWizard.save.mount.test.jsx asserts every label state, the prefilled name/description when adjusting, the inline 409 and copy-name errors, and that a user without the share permission still gets the name field but no share section.
The live counts under every wizard step, moved out of MatrixFilterWizard.jsx (#1202). Its three states (blocked, large, server-aggregated) come from matrixIsBlocked()/isServerAggregated() in MatrixFilterWizard.helpers.js, unit-tested there with inputs at the exact block boundary; what remains is number formatting and the Tailwind tone per state. MatrixFilterWizard.save.mount.test.jsx asserts the blocked and aggregated messages render for an oversized matrix.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/useWizardSave.js: The Save & share step's state and request sequence (#1202): save (POST or PUT), then share, then apply the saved matrix tagged with its id. Every decision it runs is a pure function mutated above — primaryAction/nameProblem/isDirty/savedMatrixBody in saveStepState.js, shareRequestBody/tagWithSavedMatrix in shareState.js, sendJson/isNameClash in matrixRequests.js. What is left is useState bookkeeping and await ordering, driven end to end by MatrixFilterWizard.save.mount.test.jsx: POST then share in that order, a failed share leaves the matrix saved and a retry only shares, a 409 lands on the name field and any other refusal does not, a PUT carries the lens and description.
mutationExclusions.src/components/app/MatrixWizardHost.jsx: Mounts the matrix wizard in AppMain beside the share dialog, so a matrix refetch cannot tear it down mid-edit (#1202). Its only logic is how it was asked to open — the matrix on screen, a given step, or a fresh empty matrix — a three-way prop mapping pinned case by case in MatrixWizardHost.mount.test.jsx; that the wizard survives a refetch and a view swap is pinned in AppMain.mount.test.jsx. No decision here that a mutant could change without those assertions failing.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/GridCornerControls: The grid header corner controls (#1202): the legend ? popover, the fold-all-columns toggle, and the row-axis toggles (nested groups, business roles, reset row order). It renders; what a toggle SAYS follows state computed elsewhere — columnFoldState in ./foldState.js (with its own unit test) and the flags the views pass in. GridCornerControls.mount.test.jsx pins each label, aria-pressed state, handler and hidden condition, including the mixed fold state.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/usePopover.js: Open/close state for the Export menu and the legend popover (#1202): toggle, close, and document mousedown/keydown listeners for outside-click and Escape, plus focus hand-off. Its behaviour is DOM event wiring that only means something mounted, and is pinned that way in GridCornerControls.mount.test.jsx and MatrixToolbar.mount.test.jsx (click to open, Escape and outside click close, focus moves in and back). Mutating it in isolation would test listener registration, not the behaviour the mount tests already assert.
